title: Exploratory Study on the Role of Emodin in Alleviating MPTP-Induced Neurotoxicity: A Focus on p53-Ferroptosis Signaling.
authors: Chen, Yujun; Zhao, Yuhang; Wang, Qing; Chen, Qiuchi; Chen, Xiqun; Yang, Kai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究大黄素通过p53-铁死亡信号缓解帕金森病神经毒性，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder. Emodin (EMD), which is derived from multiple Chinese medicinal herbs, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory, anti-ferroptosis, and neuroprotective effects. However, the mechanisms underlying the regulation of PD-related ferroptosis remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether EMD protects dopaminergic neurons in 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced models of PD and to elucidate its underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Potential EMD targets were predicted using SEA and Swiss databases. The PD targets were identified using the OMIM and GeneCards databases. Overlapping genes were introduced to construct protein-protein interactions (PPI) and perform Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses. Molecular docking was used to ascertain the possibility of the binding of EMD to p53 and TfR1. The stability of EMD-p53 complex was validated by using molecular dynamics simulations using the YASARA. To validate these mechanisms, we used an MPTP-induced mouse model to investigate the beneficial effects of EMD. Motor function was assessed using the open field and rotarod tests. Malondialdehyde (MDA) and iron contents in the midbrain were determined. SH-SY5Y cells were subjected with 1-methyl-4-phenyl-pyridinium (MPP(+)) or ferroptosis inducer. Ferroptosis signaling, iron metabolism, and mitochondrial superoxide levels were investigated using Western blotting, qPCR, immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry. RESULTS: Enrichment analysis revealed that the shared targets of the PD and EMD gene sets were involved in iron metabolism, with TP53 being the most connected protein in the PPI network. Molecular docking analysis suggested that EMD formed a stable complex with p53 or TfR1. Molecular Dynamics Simulation further confirmed that the interactions between EMD and p53 remained stable over time. In vivo studies demonstrated the beneficial effects of EMD in an MPTP mouse model of PD. This action was achieved by inhibiting p53 expression and mitigating ferroptosis signaling in the substantia nigra (SN). EMD similarly attenuated cell injury and ferroptosis in SH-SY5Y cells by inhibiting p53-ferroptosis signaling. In contrast, pharmacological enhancement of p53 nullified these effects in the MPP(+)-treated SH-SY5Y cells. CONCLUSION: These preliminary results indicate that EMD could exert neuroprotective effects against MPTP-induced toxicity, possibly via modulating p53-ferroptosis signaling.
abstract_zh: 背景：帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）是一种常见的神经退行性疾病。大黄素（Emodin, EMD）源自多种中药草本植物，已被报道具有抗炎、抗铁死亡和神经保护作用。然而，其调控PD相关铁死亡的机制仍不清楚。目的：探讨EMD是否在1-甲基-4-苯基-1,2,3,6-四氢吡啶（MPTP）诱导的PD模型中保护多巴胺能神经元，并阐明其潜在机制。方法：使用SEA和Swiss数据库预测EMD的潜在靶点。使用OMIM和GeneCards数据库鉴定PD靶点。将重叠基因引入以构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络，并进行基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）分析。使用分子对接确定EMD与p53和TfR1结合的可能性。使用YASARA进行分子动力学模拟验证EMD-p53复合物的稳定性。为验证这些机制，我们使用MPTP诱导的小鼠模型研究EMD的有益效应。通过开放场和旋转棒测试评估运动功能。测定中脑中的丙二醛（MDA）和铁含量。将SH-SY5Y细胞暴露于1-甲基-4-苯基吡啶（MPP(+)）或铁死亡诱导剂。使用Western blotting、qPCR、免疫荧光和流式细胞术研究铁死亡信号、铁代谢和线粒体超氧化物水平。结果：富集分析显示，PD和EMD基因集的共享靶点涉及铁代谢，其中TP53是PPI网络中连接最多的蛋白质。分子对接分析表明，EMD与p53或TfR1形成稳定复合物。分子动力学模拟进一步证实，EMD与p53之间的相互作用随时间保持稳定。体内研究表明，EMD在MPTP诱导的PD小鼠模型中具有有益效应。这一作用通过抑制黑质（SN）中p53表达和减轻铁死亡信号实现。EMD同样通过抑制p53-铁死亡信号减轻SH-SY5Y细胞中的细胞损伤和铁死亡。相反，药理学增强p53在MPP(+)处理的SH-SY5Y细胞中抵消了这些效应。结论：这些初步结果表明，EMD可能通过调节p53-铁死亡信号对MPTP诱导的毒性发挥神经保护作用。
